notes: SUCCESS. Supersedes 2026-08-13-macos-real-app-e2e, which is preserved: that run reached real Update::install but selected FULL, exposing that Update.target is updater_os() alone. DECISIONS #22 corrected platform resolution to recover the key from the url+signature Tauri selected. This run: a real Tauri app performed a real Updater::check(), derived UpdateIdentity via delta_identity(), and the runtime reported 'installed-from-delta downloaded=3884546 full=4070756'. That outcome is only constructible from UpdateSource::Delta, which attempt_delta produces only after the patch downloaded, reconstruction ran, and the rebuilt bytes matched the manifest digest -- so reconstruction is evidenced by the outcome, not inferred from the install succeeding. Signature verification then produced a VerifiedArtifact, TauriInstall handed it to real Update::install, and the installed main binary is byte-identical to the expected 1.0.1 binary (old 6890b2e5..., expected/installed 6d299c03...). Fallback scenarios (corrupt/truncated/missing patch, wrong base) now count as real delta->fallback evidence because the delta path is genuinely attempted first; they were vacuous in the previous run. Tampered-artifact scenarios refused with signature failures and installed nothing. Localhost plain HTTP was intentionally enabled for the harness via the e2e-control feature. Nothing here demonstrates production readiness, Windows, Linux, rollback resistance, or general macOS delta efficiency.
artifact_provenance: Both versions built by examples/desktop-app/e2e/build-versions.sh via 'cargo tauri build --features e2e-control'; main binaries asserted to differ before use (6890b2e5... vs 6d299c03...). Patch and manifest produced by delta-release with --target-version. Reproduce from a clean tree: rm -rf /private/tmp/delta-e2e-build && ./examples/desktop-app/e2e/build-versions.sh /private/tmp/delta-e2e-build && ./examples/desktop-app/e2e/run-e2e.sh /private/tmp/delta-e2e-build
